headline: TERRA METALS CONFIRMS 448m PGE-NICKEL-COPPER AT DANTE SOUTHWEST — All Three Pre-Collars End in Mineralisation; Maiden Southwest MRE Targeted Late 2026 (ASX: TM1)
snippet: Terra Metals (ASX: TM1) has confirmed the Southwest discovery at its Dante project in Western Australia's West Musgrave region has returned 448 metres of continuous PGE-nickel-copper sulphide mineralisation grading 0.87 g/t PGE3 (combined platinum, palladium and gold) and 0.15% nickel across three reverse-circulation pre-collars drilled over a 650-metre gap in the Southwest Main Sulphide Zone — with all three holes ending in mineralisation and deeper diamond drill tails pending assay to depths of up to 918 metres. The Southwest system is emerging as a separate growth centre from the existing 148-million-tonne Dante MRE within the same Jameson Layered Intrusion, with multiple rigs continuing extensional and infill drilling and a maiden Southwest mineral resource estimate targeted for late 2026.

headline: FREEPORT-McMoRAN BACKS AMARC'S JOY DISTRICT TO $20M — Three Rigs Chase AuRORA Porphyry Over 1.4km x 0.8km Open Footprint in British Columbia (TSXV: AHR)
snippet: Amarc Resources (TSXV: AHR / NASDAQ: AXREF) announced a $5-million budget increase for its 2026 JOY Copper-Gold District program in British Columbia, bringing the total to $20 million fully funded by Freeport-McMoRan through the AuRORA Minerals JV (Freeport 60%, Amarc 40%), as three simultaneous drill rigs advance the AuRORA Porphyry Gold-Copper-Silver Deposit — a system that 2025 drilling defined over 1.4 km by 0.8 km that remains open to expansion. The JOY District is part of Freeport's $75-million Stage 2 earn-in for an additional 10% JV interest, representing one of the largest financier commitments to a BC junior porphyry play in the current cycle — at precisely the moment when post-record copper prices have intensified the BC porphyry discovery hunt.

headline: TANZANIA CENTRAL BANK QUIETLY BOUGHT 28 TONNES OF GOLD IN 18 MONTHS — Domestic Programme Funnels ASM Output Directly to Reserves; $3.68B Deployed
snippet: Tanzania's central bank has purchased approximately 28 metric tonnes of gold valued at US$3.68 billion over the past 18 months through a government-mandated programme requiring licensed gold exporters to sell at least 20% of production to the central bank, opening more than 4,000 new formal bank accounts for small-scale miners and mineral traders in the process. The Bank of Tanzania's accumulation — virtually unreported in Western financial media until now — is part of the broader emerging-market central bank reserve diversification trend that saw 244 tonnes of gold bought globally in Q1 2026 alone; for junior gold investors, every nation-level buyer routing domestic production into reserves removes supply from the spot market while building the structural demand floor that $4,000 gold depends on.

headline: METALSOURCE MINING ADDS SECOND DRILL RIG AT SILVER HILL — 3x Drilling Capacity as Dual-Track Programme Targets Both Resource and New IP Anomalies (CSE: MSM)
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) has announced a second diamond drill rig and dedicated night shift at its Silver Hill Project in North Carolina, effectively tripling current drilling capacity through a dual-track strategy: the existing rig continues step-out resource-definition drilling along the known high-grade polymetallic system (supporting an inaugural mineral resource estimate), while the incoming second rig targets newly identified high-priority IP anomalies across the property's 2.4-kilometre strike length. The second rig is expected on site in early August, representing the largest single expansion of exploration activity at Silver Hill in the project's recent history — arriving at a moment when near-$60 silver substantially improves the economics of historically rich North Carolina polymetallic mines.

headline: TERTIARY MINERALS FINDS HIGHER-GRADE COPPER AT MUSHIMA NORTH — 45m at 0.41% Cu From 12m Depth; pXRF Silver Hits 214 g/t in Early Holes (AIM: TYM)
snippet: Tertiary Minerals (AIM: TYM / OTC: TTIRF) reported that early reverse-circulation drilling at Target A1 of its Mushima North silver-copper-zinc project in Zambia has returned 45 metres at 0.41% copper and 0.28% zinc from just 12 metres depth — including a 6-metre high-grade interval at 1.01% copper — with indicative pXRF silver readings up to 214 g/t in the first 12 holes, supporting the existing JORC Exploration Target of 15-30 million tonnes at 40-60 g/t silver equivalent. An independent competent person has visited site to review the programme ahead of a maiden JORC Mineral Resource Estimate targeted by end-2026; infill drilling continues at the density needed to support the resource calculation while step-out holes test extensions of the mineralised corridor.

headline: GOLD & SILVER GET KNOCKED DOWN — BUT NOT KNOCKED OUT: The $4,000 Floor Validated Across Multiple Sessions
snippet: FXStreet's July 20 analysis documents a week in which every macro factor pressed against precious metals — December Fed hike odds running to 80%, oil above $90 on Iran war premium, and the US dollar at multi-week highs — yet gold refused to close below $4,000 and silver held the $55 floor that institutional buyers have defended repeatedly. The piece argues that the failure of a compounding hawkish macro scenario to produce a deeper selloff is itself a bullish signal: if gold couldn't be broken below $4,000 with this combination of headwinds, the support level is harder than it looks, and the July 29 FOMC meeting is less a risk event for gold bulls and more a potential catalyst for a repricing if the Fed holds.

headline: MONEY METALS: GOLD IS TECHNICALLY OVERSOLD AND THE DEBASEMENT TRADE IS ALIVE AND WELL — RSI, COT and Moving Averages All Flash Buy Signals Simultaneously
snippet: Money Metals' July 21 editorial argues that gold's approximately 20% correction from its January 2026 all-time high has pushed the metal into extreme technical oversold territory across multiple independent indicators — RSI below 30, MACD negative divergence from the 200-day moving average, and COT net speculative longs at their lowest since 2019 — while the fundamental debasement trade (record sovereign debt, accelerating central bank buying, declining USD reserve share) that drove the original rally has not reversed. The piece frames the disconnect between technical exhaustion and intact fundamentals as the classic late-stage correction setup that has historically preceded the next leg of secular precious metals bull markets, and argues retail buyers are being handed the same entry opportunity that central banks are currently exploiting.

headline: GOLDSEEK: WHY HOLDING PHYSICAL GOLD BEATS BUYING MINING STOCKS — Data Shows Physical Outperforms GDX Over 3, 5 and 10 Years; Leverage Thesis Keeps Failing
snippet: A GoldSeek-published analysis documents the persistent underperformance of gold mining equities — as measured by GDX, GDXJ, and major producer returns — against physical gold over three, five, and ten-year time frames, challenging the 'operational leverage' thesis that repeatedly draws retail capital into miners expecting 2-3x the metal's return. The piece identifies the structural reasons leverage keeps failing in practice: rising input costs, permitting delays, management dilution through acquisitions, and the fact that mining equities are equity instruments during inflationary periods that hit margins. For investors navigating the current environment where BofA simultaneously calls miners a 'golden opportunity' while cutting the gold price target, the analysis provides a useful counterweight — the leverage thesis requires a large and sustained gold move, not a temporary rally, to actually beat physical.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM JULY OUTLOOK: THE PRICE FELL — THE CASE DIDN'T. Why $4,000 Is a Floor, Not a Ceiling
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 2026 gold outlook frames the Q2 correction — approximately 20% from the January all-time high — as entirely consistent with previous secular bull market corrections in gold (2008: -34%; 2011-2013: -44%; 2022: -21%) and argues that the underlying drivers of the 2024-2026 bull market remain intact: global sovereign debt at $353 trillion, central bank buying accelerating through Q1 2026, USD reserve share declining, and geopolitical fragmentation deepening. The analysis distinguishes between price corrections (positioning washouts in a structural bull market) and structural reversals (which require a change in the underlying drivers) and identifies the current $4,000-$4,100 zone as institutional accumulation rather than distribution — supported by State Street's $4,750-$5,500 baseline for Q1 2027 and Goldman's maintained $4,900 year-end target despite the hawkish Fed environment.
